items.before:
Para 4.2 counts any anticipated or actual ceiling, so the cumulative value of this instrument is the $9,400,000 not-to-exceed amount it has carried, not only the $8,900,000 definitized price.

Both figures land in the same class here, which is how you want to answer it: $9,400,000 is above the $9,000,000 SaP ceiling, and $8,900,000 is a non-commercial buy so the SaP rung is not open to it either. Either way the smallest rung that covers the definitization is the Class III $10M tier.

Board point: definitizing below the not-to-exceed amount does not walk you down a class - use the higher figure, say which figure you used and why, and confirm your office's practice with the Chief, C&P.

Cite: Army Warranting Program Policy v12 para 4.2 (anticipated or actual ceiling; cumulative value of the contract including the modification), Summary of Key Changes, and Table 1; RFO FAR 43 (contract modifications); RFO FAR 12.201-1 (simplified procedures apply to commercial products and commercial services).
items.after:
Para 4.2 counts any anticipated or actual ceiling, so the cumulative value of this instrument is the $9,400,000 not-to-exceed amount it has carried, not the $8,900,000 definitized price alone.

The work is non-commercial, so the SaP rung is not open to this contract at any value and the highest Class II rung available is $5,000,000. Both $9,400,000 and $8,900,000 are above it, so the definitization takes the Class III $10M tier either way and the answer does not turn on which of the two figures you use.

Board point: definitizing below the not-to-exceed amount does not walk you down a class - the contracting officer who issues the letter contract needs the warrant its ceiling calls for, and still needs it when the price is settled.

Cite: Army Warranting Program Policy v12 para 4.2 (anticipated or actual ceiling; cumulative value of the contract including the modification), Summary of Key Changes, and Table 1; RFO FAR 43 (contract modifications); RFO FAR 12.201-1 (simplified procedures apply to commercial products and commercial services).
items.source: Author's judgment call: simplified rather than removed. Kept, because the letter-contract definitization archetype was required and the difficulty-3 slot is needed; value_number $9,400,000 (the ceiling para 4.2 counts) and Class III are right. Two defects fixed. (1) The class-below exclusion was muddled: it led with '$9,400,000 is above the $9,000,000 SaP ceiling', which implies the SaP rung was in play for a buy the facts call non-commercial. SaP is a commercial-procedures authority, so the real exclusion is that the top usable Class II rung is $5,000,000 and both figures clear it. (2) The board point told the reader to 'use the higher figure ... and confirm your office's practice with the Chief, C&P' - advice the policy does not give, on a card where both figures give the same class. Now the card states the ceiling rule, shows the answer is the same either way, and makes the point that the letter contract's ceiling sets the warrant. Policy v12 Table 1 and para 4.2 (content/sources/army_warranting_policy_v12_mar2026.txt); SAT $350,000 and SaP $9,000,000 per src/data/regulations.json thresholds (sat, sap_commercial_ceiling).

unverifiable: Army Warranting Program Policy v12 is terse on how a modification is valued, and the earlier review log (content/out/games_levels_tl_cm.review.json) recorded the tension between the para 4.2 body ('include the base value, all options, any anticipated or actual ceiling values, plus the absolute value of a modification') and the Summary of Key Changes entry for 4.2 ('it must be equal to or greater than the cumulative value of the contract including the modification'). The app has since settled on the cumulative reading - existing TL63 now carries value_number $69,600,000 ($64,000,000 + $5,600,000) and TL64 $2,310,000 - and these 30 cards follow it, as the authoring task directed. On the discarded modification-only reading three new cards would change class: TL101 ($260,000, Class I instead of III), TL102 ($12,000,000, Class III instead of IV) and TL103 ($0). Nothing changed here; recording it so the owner sees which cards depend on the settled reading.

Letter-contract definitization (TL104) is not addressed by name in Policy v12. The card values the instrument at the $9,400,000 not-to-exceed amount on the strength of 'any anticipated or actual ceiling' in para 4.2. The definitized price of $8,900,000 gives the same class, so nothing in the set turns on the choice, and the rewritten card now says so instead of sending the reader to ask.

Cite numbers for indefinite-delivery contract types, requirements contracts, time-and-materials ceilings and letter contracts (TL91, TL92, TL96, TL98) are left at part level, 'RFO FAR 16 (types of contracts)'. content/out/crosswalk_far_1_19.json verifies the RFO renumbering inside subpart 16.5 (16.506, 16.507, 16.508) but not sections for these contract types, and the AGENT_BRIEF rule is to keep an unverified number out rather than guess one.
